answer: A zero-knowledge nullifier protocol resists Sybil swarms by requiring each agent to prove possession of an unspent carrier eSIM or bank token via a zk-SNARK, publishing a deterministic nullifier at the onboarding inlet to block reuse. Because bots easily pass linguistic tests like writing a sonnet and otherwise branch like a vine, attackers must incur the scarce cost of acquiring distinct real-world accounts per identity. One limitation is that corrupt issuers can still mint hidden bulk tokens.
